mbm-1201.clue: I went back for the empty space.
mbm-1201.quote: A museum took my favorite bronze dog away for cleaning. I sketched its empty plinth, complete with the little square of dust where its back paw had stood. When it returned I drew the dog beside it.

mbm-1202.clue: We aim for the striped shadow.
mbm-1202.quote: My friends and I play flying disc across the shadows of an old fence. Whoever lands it on a dark stripe picks the next target. At sunset our whole playing field stretches down the block.

mbm-1203.clue: I keep the paint off the apple.
mbm-1203.quote: I painted a red apple until the light turned it nearly black on one side. My sister waited the whole afternoon to eat it. When she finally took a bite I painted the white crescent too.

mbm-1204.clue: I made my first stamp from a button.
mbm-1204.quote: I pressed a coat button into damp leather and discovered a perfect little rosette. The pattern now runs around the edge of my tool roll. The button still holds my coat shut.

mbm-1205.clue: I let the rain finish one painting.
mbm-1205.quote: A shower spotted my watercolor of a greenhouse garden. When the drops dried they looked like little flowers beyond the eave. I signed it in pencil where the paper stayed dry.

mbm-1206.clue: I put the quilt on backwards for a reason.
mbm-1206.quote: Every person in our group signed the back of a patch before I joined the blanket. We spread it signatures-up at the reunion. Nobody wanted to sit on a friend’s name.

mbm-1207.clue: I keep binoculars beside my mixing bowl.
mbm-1207.quote: A pair of swallows feeds its young above the bakery window. I watch between batches of bread. One chick has a louder lunch bell than the timer in our kitchen.

mbm-1208.clue: I pinched the stepping-stones before the pond was blue.
mbm-1208.quote: Before firing I pinched a row of little dents into my clay dish. The blue glaze pooled in each one. When it came out of the kiln I’d made a pond with a whole row of stepping-stones.

mbm-1209.clue: I measured the squares against a book cover.
mbm-1209.quote: My reading quilt has a patch for every book Mum read aloud to us. I stitched a little silver key on the one she read twice. None of us could bear to leave that garden.

mbm-1210.clue: The smallest part of my train is a star.
mbm-1210.quote: The retired conductor let me try his old brass punch at the railway museum. I punched a tiny star in a paper train I’d drawn. He asked if the passenger had paid for a return.

mbm-1211.clue: I made a bowl that’s scared of the dark.
mbm-1211.quote: I cut little moon-shaped openings around a clay bowl and put a candle inside. The moons scatter over the table. My brother and I set three marbles among them. He calls it our private universe.

mbm-1212.clue: I save one spot on my dance card.
mbm-1212.quote: There’s one spot on my dance card for whoever is sitting alone when the last song starts. The last time I filled it my partner taught me a turn I’ve practiced every day since.

mbm-1213.clue: I crochet my own soft dice.
mbm-1213.quote: I made big yarn dice for a board game in the park. One rolled under a bench and a toddler hugged it. We played the rest of the afternoon with the little ones.

mbm-1214.clue: I have to shake my shoe out after a good swim.
mbm-1214.quote: My little cousin counts my pool laps, but she only knows the numbers up to four. Every fourth lap she drops a pebble in my sandal. I rattled all the way to the changing room on Saturday.

mbm-1215.clue: The frosting washed out just enough.
mbm-1215.quote: My niece spilled pink frosting across the white cloth I was going to quilt. I washed it and cut the faint pink patches into flower petals. The blanket will always remember her sixth birthday.

mbm-1216.clue: I heard the cheering before I saw the dock.
mbm-1216.quote: I came through the last turn on water skis with the sun in my eyes. My friends had made a cardboard finish arch on the dock. I coasted past and saw a star of sunlight in its shadow.

mbm-1217.clue: My shirt won a second prize.
mbm-1217.quote: The county fair offered a ribbon for neat eating at the berry contest. A tiny splash on my collar looked exactly like a butterfly. The art teacher drew antennae on it and gave me her own prize.

mbm-1218.clue: I paint the feather over the fold.
mbm-1218.quote: I painted a peacock eye across the folds of a fan. Shut, it becomes a blue stripe. Open it quickly and the eye seems to blink. I spent a whole lunch break making my sister laugh with it.

mbm-1219.clue: I have a very patient onion.
mbm-1219.quote: At the market I tried to juggle three beanbags and an onion for the stallholder. One beanbag went under his cart. The onion stayed tucked under my chin through my entire bow.

mbm-1220.clue: I made a little leather roof for my keys.
mbm-1220.quote: I stitched the key pouch to look like my grandparents’ house. The keys hang in the doorway on a brass ring. Dad always knocks on the flap before he borrows one.

mbm-1221.clue: I know the secret to my aunt’s cheering.
mbm-1221.quote: At the noodle contest she waved a paper fan painted with one enormous noodle. I laughed so hard I had to put my chopsticks down. We both agreed I’d already won lunch.

mbm-1222.clue: I let the windmill decide the color.
mbm-1222.quote: At the mini-golf shop I bought a pencil for my scorecard. Its red eraser matched the windmill blades exactly. My friend took a photo that makes it look like I’m erasing a whole blade.

mbm-1223.clue: Our raft made a postcard on its own.
mbm-1223.quote: A wet maple leaf stuck to the yellow bow all the way downriver. At the takeout it left a perfect print in the mud. I photographed it before we washed the boat.

mbm-1224.clue: I put the shoreline where the seam went.
mbm-1224.quote: My first blue cloth was too short for a full quilt, so I joined a sandy strip along one edge. Mum found a boat-print scrap. Suddenly the shortage had given us a beach.

mbm-1225.clue: I don’t dog-ear a good joke.
mbm-1225.quote: I slip a little yellow paper flag beside words that make me laugh aloud. When I pass a book to a friend, the flags stick up like grass. Sometimes they send it back even grassier.
